name: Capsule Network
analogy: Think of it as a chart reader who spots parts and then checks that the parts agree on the whole. A long lower wick, a small body and a follow-through bar each vote for which larger pattern they belong to, and the pattern with the most agreement wins.

steps.title: Detect small pieces
steps.description: The first layers look at the raw window of bars and detect small local pieces, such as a long wick, a gap or a small-bodied bar. Each piece is described by a short list of numbers, not a single score.
steps.inExample: In a 20-bar MNQ window the first layer finds a long lower wick at bar 17 and a strong up-bar at bar 19.

steps.title: Wrap each piece in a capsule
steps.description: Every detected piece becomes a capsule, a small group of numbers. The length of the group says how likely the piece is to be present, and its direction encodes details such as size and position.
steps.inExample: The wick capsule has a length of 90 on a scale of 0 to 100, meaning it is almost certainly there, and its direction encodes a wick of about 30 points.

steps.title: Let each piece guess the whole
steps.description: Each small capsule predicts what every larger capsule should look like if that piece belonged to it, using learned transformations. A wick might predict what a hammer-and-follow-through reversal would look like.
steps.inExample: The wick and the up-bar both predict a bullish reversal setup of about 50 points in total height.

steps.title: Route by agreement
steps.description: The pieces send their output mainly to the larger capsule whose prediction they agree with. This is repeated a few times, so pieces that agree reinforce each other and pieces that disagree are dropped from that group.
steps.inExample: After three rounds, the wick and up-bar send most of their weight to the reversal capsule, and little to the breakout capsule.

steps.title: Read the strength of each larger capsule
steps.description: The larger capsules, one per class such as reversal, breakout or none, end with a length that works as a confidence. A long capsule means the model has found a consistent arrangement of parts for that class.
steps.inExample: On a scale of 0 to 100, the reversal capsule has a length of 78, the breakout capsule 21, and the no-pattern capsule 10.

steps.title: Train with a margin
steps.description: During training, the correct class is pushed to have a long capsule and the wrong classes are pushed to be short, with a margin so that the model is not rewarded for being only barely right.
steps.inExample: On a training window labeled reversal, the reversal capsule is pushed past 90 and the others below 10.

useFor.example: Detecting a rejection wick followed by a strong close on MNQ 5-minute bars, with the size of the setup carried in the capsule.
Combining several local motifs, such as an inside bar and a breakout bar, into one higher-level setup such as a compression breakout.
Using one capsule each for trending, ranging and volatile states, and reading the length as how sure the model is.
Treating a window where no class capsule is long as structurally unfamiliar and standing down.

avoidWhen: You need a quick, robust baseline; capsule networks are slower to train and touchy to tune, and a convolutional or tree model on the same features is the safer first try.
The input is a plain table of indicators; capsules shine on structured parts-and-wholes data like patterns, not on a flat row of unrelated numbers.

example.scenario: A capsule network trained to label 20-bar windows of MNQ 5-minute bars as reversal, breakout or no pattern is shown a window that ends with a long lower wick and a strong up-bar.

input.summary: A window of 20 bars with open, high, low, close and volume, scaled to the window.

fields.name: window length
fields.meaning: How many 5-minute bars the model sees.

fields.name: lower wick at bar 17
fields.meaning: The distance from the bar's low up to its body, showing a sharp rejection of lower prices.

fields.name: up-bar at bar 19
fields.meaning: A strong bullish bar following the rejection.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical recent high-to-low travel of a bar.

fields.name: volume on the up-bar against average

output.summary: A length for each class capsule and the class chosen.

fields.name: reversal capsule length
fields.meaning: The model's confidence that the window is a reversal setup.

fields.name: breakout capsule length
fields.meaning: Low confidence that the window is a breakout.

fields.name: no-pattern capsule length
fields.meaning: Low confidence that the window is unremarkable.

fields.name: chosen class
fields.meaning: The class with the longest capsule, above the model's acceptance margin.

example.reading: A length of 78 out of 100 says the parts agree on a reversal shape, but it only labels the pattern; it does not say what happens next. Treat it as a filter or a feature, then measure what MNQ actually did after such windows, net of costs, across walk-forward folds.
